01 / A very human impulse

First, we drew.
Then, we caught the light.

From a hand on a cave wall to a sensor in your pocket, we’ve always wanted to hold on to what we see.

02 / A little understanding goes a long way

Light. Time. A point of view.

No experience required. Just three ideas to start seeing your photographs differently.

THE APERTURETry it yourself ↙
LIGHT / THE FIRST INGREDIENT
f/2.8 · More lightf/16 · Less light

At f/5.6, the opening admits 4× the light of f/11.

01

Let the light in.

Aperture controls the lens opening. It changes how much light enters and how much of the scene appears sharp.

Understand aperture ↗
02

Give it a moment.

The shutter decides how long light is recorded. A fraction of a second can freeze a moment—or let it move.

Explore time & exposure ↗
03

Choose what matters.

Focus and framing turn a scene into your photograph. Different finders invite different ways of looking.

Discover focus & framing ↗
